recipes.name: Ham and Cheese Quiche
ingredients_raw: 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch single crust pie

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat together flour, salt, half-and-half and eggs in a medium bowl.

Place Swiss cheese flat in the pie crust. Arrange spinach evenly over Swiss cheese, then cover with mushrooms. Pour the flour and egg mixture over mushrooms. Cover with flaked ham and top with Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven 45 to 55 minutes, until surface is golden brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Cheese Quiche
raw_recipe.description: A Swiss cheese, spinach and mushroom layer is topped with a thick egg mixture, a layer of ham and a sprinkling of Cheddar. This robust pie is tucked into an oven and baked for an hour. It ‘s perfect for lunch or brunch.

review.reviewBody: This was so easy and tasted fabulous! The only thing I did differently was use up 4 slices of swiss cheese(two on the bottom layer and two in the egg mixture)and used sandwich ham meat, cut up which I combined with the egg mixture as well. The pie crust didn't really cook thoroughly, I'm not sure if it's because I didn't cook it long enough (45 mins), but it turned soggy, so we just ate the filling. I think next time, we'll prebake the pie crust and then fill it. Another thing I'd do differently is instead of layer the swiss on the bottom, I'll just combine it all with the eggs and then use about 1/4 cup of the egg on the bottom layer and then add ham to the egg mixture and top it off with that. Other than that, it's perfect.

This tasted fantastic and was so easy! I used fresh chopped spinach, fresh portobello shrooms (as I did not have canned shrooms or frozen spinach) and added chopped scallions. I also used Pillsbury ready made pie crust and baked it for 10 minutes at 425 prior to putting the mixture in. It cooked at 350 for 1 hr in my oven and it was perfect! This is now in the rotation!

I've made this quiche multiple and each time it always gets rave reviews. I serve it with a simple side salad with a homemade citrus/olive oil vingerette. 

I have made the following alterations so it lends itself to my families taste and diet:

I use fat free half and half, 4 eggs, 2oz grated swiss, 1 deep dish pie crust, 1 small box frozen spinach, 1 cup fresh sauteed in olive oil mushrooms, 7oz cubed ham steak, and 1oz shredded cheddar. The salt and the flour remain the same. I also defrost the pie crust and pre-bake it for 5 mintues at 350.

I find that if I use an entire box of frozen spinach I need the extra egg to hold all the veggies together, yet the extra egg is too much liquid for a normal pie crust, so a deep dish pie crust is necessary.

It's still hearty, rich, comfort food and with these alterations you can calorically eat 1/4 of the quiche and not break the bank. Plus we always have leftovers and it reheats nicely. Delicious!

Made this a day ahead and refrigerated it so I could throw it in the oven on Christmas morning. Everyone LOVED it! Will definitely make this again and again. I used fresh mushrooms and sauteed them to get the water out as some reviews said the crust was undercooked and soggy. This was not the case for mine. Also used frozen drained spinach and shredded Swiss cheese, not slices. Mixed Swiss in with 1/4 egg mixture and put that it the crust first. Layered the spinach next, then the mushrooms then sliced lunch meat ham. Finally added the rest of the egg mixture with the cheddar cheese mixed in 
 Turned out perfectly. Very flavorful.

This was absolutely delicious! I made just a couple of changes. I baked the crusts for 10 minutes prior to filling as suggested by other reviews. I doubled the recipe and also doubled the about of swiss cheese. Glad I did! Also added some diced green onions. I also used leftover ham instead of canned. I also didn't have very much half and half so I substituted whole milk. I will definitely make this again!
I used 3 pieces of Swiss cheese and cubed baked ham. I sauted garlic, mushrooms and spinach, poured the eggs mixture over that and sprinkled some cheddar on top

Yum. The filling was made almost to the letter except for the following. I added 1/4 cup of chopped red onion. I did not have the whole amount of the half and half, so I topped up with evaporated milk. I had two eggs so I added egg white. Instead of the crust (higher in fat), I sprayed the pie plate with PAM, and pressed in 1 1/2 cups of shredded potatoes onto the bottom of the pie plate. Sprayed the potatoes with more PAM and baked for 15 minutes before filling. Delicious. Thanks for the recipe.

Wow! This was fantastic! I used three slices of cheddar ( that was what I had on hand) and they nicely covered the crust. I upped the chopped fresh spinach to 1.5 cups (more veggies), used 4oz fresh sliced mushrooms ( sautéed in a little butter), 3/4 to 1 c chopped left over ham, and 1/2 c shredded mozzarella (what I had). I layered the spinach on top of the sliced cheese, according to the recipe, which really helped keep the crust crisp and not at all soggy. I then combined the ham and mushrooms with the egg mixture. I finished it off with a light sprinkling of shaved Parmesan. This was soo easy, and the directions were simple. The result was fabulous! My daughter (who up to now wanted no part of cooking) asked if I could show her how to make it! A new household favorite!

I gave it a five star only because of my tweeks to the recipe. I made this for the first time yesterday. Used evaporated milk, instead of half & half. I used shredded swiss on bottom of pie. I sauted fresh mushrooms, onion, garlic and fresh coursely chopped spinach. A must to sautee prior to adding, it makes for a more tastey and firmer quiche....Delicious.

This recipe was super easy for my first quiche. I used a premade refrigerated pie crust and rolled it into the pan. I made a few modifications overall. 1. I shredded block swiss and coated the bottom. 2. I cut up the spinach and cut up fresh mushrooms and added those on top. 3. I used leftover ham and cut it into squares. My husband ate 3 pieces and said it was fantastic. My extremely picky 11-year-old ate a slice and said it was OK. and finished her slice. ( this means she liked it haha!)

I've made this a million times over the last couple of years. It was 5 stars when I followed the recipe exactly (I only rate on the exact recipe as submitted!!!)... It is now 6 stars since I've made minor modifications over time to my taste. I have learned that I like it even better when I saute chopped deli ham (or bacon), diced onions and mushrooms in butter to get that browned taste before sprinkling it all over the top of the egg mixture. I also add a few dashes of garlic powder and dry mustard powder to the egg mixture. Tip: if you use frozen spinach, be sure to thaw and squeeze/drain all excess water out. I always double this for leftovers. Thank you!
I for the most part like the recipe. What other cheese can you use instead of Swiss not a big fan of it

I've made this many times with different ingredients. Bacon and cheddar, pepperoni with mozzerella and cheddar, and ham with various cheeses. All great!! I usually add onions and bell peppers to my quiches.
Increased Swiss cheese to 4 slices and combined shredded cheddar cheese with mozzarella cheese.
Good! Added some chopped red onion and used fresh mushrooms and leftover Easter ham.
Easy enough, I've made it a few times when we have family overnight.

This recipe is super simple as everyone has mentioned. I used 4 slices of swiss (you can't have some slices with and without swiss!) and also sauteed the spinach and mushrooms. I don't think the mushrooms are necessary. I added a splash of balsamic when sauteeing this spinach (a lot more spinach, BTW, maybe 3x as much - we could all use a little more spinach in our lives!) and added a few shakes of thyme, garlic powder and black pepper the second time I made it. But, great recipe!
This has become a family favorite! Delicious just as it is!
My first attempt at making quiche. Delicious! I followed the recipe exactly.

The flavor was wonderful. I do agree with other reviewers that crust was soggy. May try pre-baking crust a bit or use frozen spinach as suggested. The addition of green onion also sounds like a good idea. May also add an additional egg.
